vision: Build a plan-driven bug attribution agent with internal governance. The system separates concerns into three pipelines: (1) Input Pipeline — deterministic extraction and candidate retrieval at zero LLM cost; (2) Agent Pipeline — LLM plans, examines, and attributes within an InvestigationBrief, governed by an investigation harness with rules and skills; (3) Evaluation Pipeline — oracle scores output. The agent receives a CandidateSet (not raw repo access), operates within completion criteria (not just budget), produces structured InvestigationTraces for learning, and improves over time via skills derived from traces. Evaluated via Hit@k, MRR, D3, D6, and Retrieval Recall against ApacheJIT ground truth.
direction: ARCHITECTURE V4.2: PROVEN at scale (n=20, 6 cloud models). Best: gpt-5.3-codex Hit@5=0.500, MRR=0.400, 62s/case — ties claude-sonnet-4-6 Hit@5=0.500, MRR=0.354, 125s/case but 2x faster. Budget models viable: claude-haiku-4-5 (0.450), gpt-5.4-nano (0.400). gemini-3-flash (0.000) and composer-2.5 (0.400 partial, latency-aborted) not viable. Pipeline ceiling appears to be Hit@5=0.500 at n=20 — bottleneck is Recall@100=0.700 (6 cases never enter the funnel). Prior n=5 baseline (0.800) was overfit to easy cases.

invariants.temporal_bound: Temporal bound (COMMIT_B~1) constrains the ENTIRE system — input pipeline retrieval and agent tools. In eval mode, bound comes from fix_hash.
invariants.llm_reasons_scripts_retrieve: Scripts own retrieval (candidate set assembly) and evidence verification. LLM owns planning, examination reasoning, and attribution.
invariants.agent_is_governed: The investigation harness governs the LLM. The harness manages state, transitions, and completion criteria.
invariants.observable_by_design: Every investigation produces a structured InvestigationTrace. Traces are the substrate for skill emergence.
invariants.ground_truth: GroundTruthGraph provides bug_hash from commit_links.csv. SZZ-based labeling has known noise — Hit@5 is primary metric, not Hit@1.

tasks.name: V4.2 model comparison: local models n=5 eval
tasks.scope: Run n=5 eval (subset with ExamRecall=true) on multiple local models to find best candidate for full n=20 re-eval. Models: qwen3.6:35b-a3b (MoE, thinking OFF), qwen3:8b (thinking ON, max_tokens=16384), gemma3:12b-it-q8_0. Compare Hit@5, conversion rate, speed. Pick best for full re-eval.

tasks.name: Scaled eval across 6 cloud models via Cursor SDK

Models: claude-sonnet-4-6 (baseline), claude-haiku-4-5, gpt-5.4-nano, gpt-5.3-codex, gemini-3-flash, composer-2.5. Compare Hit@5, MRR, avg latency, cost/case. Implement automatic early-stopping.

subtasks.name: Parameterize CursorSDKProvider model in get_provider
subtasks.scope: Add a `model` kwarg to get_provider() so callers can request a specific Cursor SDK model. When CURSOR_API_KEY is set and model is specified, pass it through to CursorSDKProvider(model=...). The existing default (claude-sonnet-4-6) stays unchanged when no model is specified. Touch: llm_providers.py only.

subtasks.name: Early-stopping monitor module
subtasks.scope: New module (likely src/commit_investigator/eval/run_monitor.py or similar) that tracks per-model running metrics and checks all 5 hard-stop rules after each case. Inputs: case result dict (has elapsed_ms, hit_at_5, status, estimated cost). Outputs: continue/abort decision with reason string. Also tracks global spend across models for the $50 budget cap. Must be stateful per model (rolling windows, cumulative counters) but simple — a class with an update() method returning a verdict.

subtasks.name: Multi-model runner script
subtasks.scope: New script scripts/run_scaled_eval.py. Orchestrates: (1) load eval cases once, (2) iterate models sequentially, (3) for each model: create CursorSDKProvider with that model, create run folder, run cases calling run_single_case() from run_scoped_eval.py, check monitor after each case, write per-model summary.json on completion or abort. Support checkpoint/resume: persist progress to a checkpoint file in the run folder, skip completed cases on restart, skip fully-completed models. Accept CLI args: --models (comma-separated, default all 6), --max-n (case limit), --resume (path to previous run to continue). Import run_single_case from run_scoped_eval — do NOT duplicate pipeline logic.

subtasks.name: Comparison report generator
subtasks.scope: After all models complete (or abort), produce a combined comparison summary. Output: results/{timestamp}-scaled-eval-comparison/comparison.json with per-model rows (model, hit_at_5, mrr, n_completed, n_aborted, avg_latency_s, cost_per_case, total_cost, abort_reason). Also print a formatted ASCII table to stdout. Can be a function in the runner script or a separate small module — builder decides. Must handle partial results (some models aborted).

subtasks.name: Fix resume bugs (monitor state, duplicate folders, checkpoint consistency)
subtasks.scope: Three resume-related bugs: (1) EarlyStopMonitor state is not restored on resume — prior case results must be replayed through monitor.update() so hard-stop rules have correct history. Add a replay_checkpoint() method or similar. (2) _run_model() unconditionally calls create_run_folder() — on resume, reuse the existing model folder from checkpoint instead of creating a new timestamped folder (store model_dir path in checkpoint). (3) Abort-triggering case is in case_results but not in local completed_keys — after the break, the checkpoint save at line 311 derives completed_keys from status=='completed' which correctly includes it, so this is actually fine for checkpoint. But the monitor sees it counted while completed_keys doesn't, creating a discrepancy within the same run. Move completed_keys.add() before the abort check, or document the intentional gap. Touch: run_scaled_eval.py, run_monitor.py.

subtasks.name: Tune early-stop thresholds for n=20 dataset
subtasks.scope: perf_min_cases=20 is useless — there are exactly 20 eval cases, so the performance floor only fires after ALL cases complete. Lower to 10 for meaningful early detection. Also: the flat $0.000003/token cost rate is model-agnostic and based on word count, not real tokens. Since all calls go through Cursor SDK (subscription-based, not direct API billing), the cost numbers in the comparison report are rough proxies at best. Options: (A) add per-model cost multipliers as a config dict, (B) accept the limitation and add a clear note in comparison.json output that costs are estimated, or (C) query actual Cursor usage after the run. Recommend option B — accuracy isn't critical since the $15/$50 caps are safety nets, not billing controls. Touch: run_monitor.py (threshold), run_scaled_eval.py (cost note in comparison output).

subtasks.name: Add model validation pre-flight check
subtasks.scope: Before starting the run, validate all requested model IDs against the Cursor SDK. Use Cursor.models.list() (from cursor_sdk) to fetch valid model slugs and warn/abort if any requested model is not in the list. This prevents wasting time on models that will just error out on every case. Handle gracefully: if models.list() fails (network, auth), log a warning and proceed without validation. Touch: run_scaled_eval.py only.

Early-stopping saved ~50% time on gemini-3-flash (perf floor) and composer-2.5 (latency ceiling). Pipeline ceiling is Recall@100=0.700. Results in results/2026-06-18T14-41-scaled-eval/ (main), results/2026-06-18T17-06-scaled-eval/ (codex), results/2026-06-18T17-30-scaled-eval/ (sonnet).

tasks.name: Trace analysis: sonnet vs codex failure modes and improvement hypotheses
tasks.scope: Analyze investigation traces from the n=20 scaled eval for claude-sonnet-4-6 and gpt-5.3-codex. Both hit 10/20 — the SAME 10 cases. Focus on the 10 misses: (1) How many are Recall@100 misses (bug never in candidate set)? (2) How many survive to ExamRecall but fail attribution? (3) What patterns distinguish hits from misses? (4) Are misses due to weak retrieval, bad triage, poor investigation reasoning, or noisy ground truth? Produce hypotheses for what could lift Hit@5 from 0.500 toward 0.700+. Output: structured analysis document with per-case miss breakdown, failure taxonomy, and ranked improvement hypotheses.
tasks.note: Both top models hit the same 10 cases — suggests the pipeline has a structural ceiling, not a model reasoning ceiling. Recall@100=0.700 means 6 cases are lost before the LLM even sees them. This spike determines whether the next investment is retrieval (lift Recall@100) or investigation (lift ExamRecall→Hit@5 conversion).
